mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Good Standing of foreign corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction corporate registry (e.g., State Administration for Market Regulation, PRC, if corporate GP is Chinese)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via competent authority in country of issuance (Canada has been a party to the Apostille Convention since January 11, 2024; consular legalization required only for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incumbency listing directors, officers and authorized signatories of corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Secretary / legal counsel of the foreign General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in jurisdiction of origin, then apostille at federal/central competent authority (e.g., MLAT / Foreign Affairs Office) where Hague applies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of passport photo pages for all ultimate beneficial owners and General Partner controllers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified notary public in the residence country of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus apostille or consular legalization depending on country of origin; may be waived by the Alberta registry agent relying on KYC equivalence only if the entity is a regulated financial institution's client

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing Alberta resident registered office and filing service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Prospective General Partner of the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and, if foreign executed and requested by registry agent, apostilled

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, General Partner principals, and designated signatories against OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian autonomous sanctions under SEMA, the Magnitsky sanctions list, and domestic FINTRAC/police watchlists; any positive PEP match triggers enhanced due diligence and, if the PEP is a foreign political figure, mandatory senior management approval and enhanced monitoring under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance; Canada imposes no general prohibition on servicing foreign PEPs, but transaction monitoring must be risk-based and documented

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) via licensed Registry Agent; NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report must be obtained through an authorized Alberta corporate registry service provider; no direct public self-service via the Alberta Government is available for entity filing
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate and limited partnership names in Alberta must use English or French alphabetic characters and standard Roman script; names may include accents but permit only letters, numbers, spaces and limited punctuation; a NUANS report is required for limited partnership registration to verify that the proposed name is not confusingly similar to existing Alberta registered names, federal names, and registered trademarks; Chinese characters are not permitted in the legal registered name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS name search report is valid for 90 days from the date of search; no fee-based extension exists in Alberta, so a fresh NUANS search and fee payment are required if filing occurs after 90 days; if the proposed name is rejected by the Registrar on distinctiveness or confusion grounds, the applicant must first submit a revised name with a new NUANS report; formal objection or appeal against a name registration decision may be filed with the Registrar of Companies under the Business Names Registration Act, and further judicial review lies to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within the applicable limitation period

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted if a physical street address in Alberta is designated for service of process and the virtual office provider maintains a real reception and document handling capacity; a post office box alone is prohibited; the Alberta registrar will accept a virtual office address for a limited partnership engaged in engineering CAD outsourcing provided the address is not merely a mail forwarding point and can receive legal process; standard industry practice is accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low 5-10% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk offshore professional services LP in the current regulatory cycle; inspection probability concentrates on registrations that trigger FINTRAC enforcement or Alberta securities compliance; no routine on-site verification is performed at formation if all filings are executed through a licensed registry agent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c P-3, as amended: s. 51 (registration of limited partnerships), s. 52 (declaration contents), s. 53 (registration certificate), s. 57 (registered office in Alberta), s. 66 (annual return); administered alongside the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) for a corporate general partner and the federal Canada Revenue Agency registration regime for the Business Number.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP-2 – Registration of a Limited Partnership (Statutory Declaration), filed under the Partnership Act (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Partnership Act (Alberta) imposes no minimum paid-up capital or statutory escrow/blocked deposit account for a limited partnership. Capital contributions are fixed exclusively by the Limited Partnership Agreement and may be funded in cash or property by wire transfer; the registered office in Alberta must be maintained at all times.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF BIM INFRASTRUCTURE LP (ALBERTA), ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A FIRST MEETING. 1. REGISTERED OFFICE: The Partnership's registered office is set at the office of [Trust Company], Calgary, Alberta. 2. CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS: Initial limited partner subscriptions, totalling not less than [CA$____], are accepted and must be transferred within 30 days. 3. GOVERNANCE: The Limited Partnership Agreement is ratified; the General Partner is authorized to manage Partnership affairs. 4. OFFICERS AND AGENTS: [Name] is appointed Managing Partner; [Law Firm] is appointed Legal Representative, authorized to execute and file Form LP-2 with the Alberta Corporate Registry and open the partnership's bank account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Partnership Name Search and NUANS Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized NUANS search providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an electronic NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) search on the proposed name 'BIM Infrastructure LP' and two alternates. Verify that the name ends with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' and contains no statutorily prohibited or misleading terms. Reserve the approved name for 90 days and ensure the Form LP-2 filing occurs before reservation expiry.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and two alternate names
Written authorization from the intending general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a distinctiveness or confusion objection, obtain a written consent from the prior registrant or select an alternate name from the search report and resubmit for reservation without loss of priority if filed within the 90-day window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private instrument executed between the General Partner and Limited Partners under supervision of Alberta legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) covering capital commitments, profit and loss allocations, management authority of the general partner, transfer restrictions, admission of additional limited partners, and dissolution events. Obtain each limited partner's identity and tax residence documentation. The general partner's board resolution ratifies the LPA and the subscription schedule.
required_dossiers: Unanimous written consent/resolution of the general partner's board
Subscription schedules and KYC/residence documentation of all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscribing partner fails KYC or payment, amend the subscription schedule and re-execute the relevant signature pages; the LPA remains binding on all executing parties and no government cure is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Form LP-2 – Registration of a Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta Corporate Registry (online corporate registry system or paper submission through authorized Alberta Service Centres)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form LP-2 accompanied by the reserved NUANS report stating the exact partnership name, the Alberta registered office address and contact, full particulars of each general partner, indication that the partnership has at least one general and one limited partner, and the statement of business scope (ISIC 7110 engineering drafting and BIM services). Pay the CAD 100 statutory fee (approx. USD 74) and obtain the Certificate of Registration confirming the limited partnership is validly constituted.
required_dossiers: Form LP-2 (Registration of a Limited Partnership)
Consent of the registered office provider with Alberta address
General partner particulars and certificate of corporate status (if the general partner is a corporation)
Payment confirmation of the CAD 100 registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Service Alberta issues a Request for Information or a Rejection Notice, cure the deficiency within the stated period by filing Form LP-3 (Amendment of Limited Partnership) or providing the missing declaration/consent; expedited re-filing is available through the Priority Services channel to protect the 90-day name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax Registrations – CRA Business Number and Program Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Partnership for a CRA Business Number (BN) using the Certificate of Registration and the executed LPA. Open a GST/HST account under the Excise Tax Act (Alberta) noting that exported CAD/BIM services to non-resident clients are generally zero-rated; open a payroll account if employees are engaged. Confirm each partner's Canadian-residency status for withholding and reporting obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration issued by Service Alberta
Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) / RC1A for partnership programmes
Government-issued identification and foreign TINs of all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If BN issuance is delayed, contact the CRA Business Registration line (1-800-959-5525) to obtain an interim reference number and upload the outstanding documents; duplicate or mis-filed program accounts are corrigible by filing Form RC1 amendments online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupancy, Fire Safety, OHS Clearance, and Annual Return Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs / Safety Codes Council (municipal fire marshal); Alberta Occupational Health and Safety; Service Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure the office leasehold occupancy permit and fire safety plan approval under the Alberta Fire Code before commencing operations. For a headcount of 20 or more, implement a written OHS program under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Alberta) including hazard assessment and first aid. File the Partnership's annual return with Service Alberta Corporate Registry before the registration anniversary each year to maintain good standing.
required_dossiers: Leasehold occupancy approval / building permit under the Safety Codes Act (Alberta)
Alberta Fire Code compliance certificate or fire safety plan approval
OHS hazard assessment and emergency response records
Annual return filing confirmation from Service Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to file the annual return results in a Notice of Default and possible dissolution after one year; remedy by filing the overdue annual return with a Statement of Disclosure and, if dissolved, applying for restoration under the Partnership Act within the applicable statutory period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – office-based BIM/CAD drafting creates no manufacturing operation in Alberta. Adjunct regulatory reference: Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) governs reserved engineering practice; an APEGA Permit to Practice is required only if the Partnership offers reserved engineering services to clients within Alberta, which the offshore outsourcing commercial model excludes.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required. Reference: Engineering and Geoscience Professions Act (Alberta) – exemption for administrative drafting services that do not constitute the practice of professional engineering in Alberta.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no activity listed under the Activities Designation Regulation (A.R. 276/2003) of the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (Alberta) is triggered by office-based CAD/BIM drafting; neither EIA registration nor a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered: zero industrial wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste generation. General obligations: compliance with municipal wastewater by-laws for office sanitary discharge; adherence to Alberta Tier 1 Soil and Groundwater Remediation Guidelines if any future leasehold remediation is required; electronic and computer waste routed through municipal e-waste recycling programmes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: compliance with the Alberta Fire Code (National Fire Code – 2023 Alberta Edition) including municipal fire safety plan approval for the office leasehold. Structural/Occupancy: building occupancy permit under the Safety Codes Act (Alberta) and, where applicable, structural load verification by a licensed engineer for high-density server racks or heavy equipment. Occupational Health: compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Alberta) and OHS Code – hazard assessment, first aid arrangements, and emergency response plan; a documented OHS programme is mandatory for employers with 20 or more workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – GST/HST, payroll and income tax administration; Business Registration Online portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business.html) and Represent a Client for non-resident entities. In Alberta, provincial partnership registration and corporate registry services are administered by Service Alberta through the Alberta Corporate Registration System (CORES).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Alberta Limited Partnership claiming GST zero-rating on exported CAD/BIM services, the LP must first be properly created and registered under Alberta's Partnership Act. The LP or its designated partner then obtains a federal Business Number (BN) from CRA by enrolling through Business Registration Online (BRO), by mail using Form RC148, or by telephone. The application must include the partnership's legal name, Alberta registration number, address, fiscal year, and the completion of the GST/HST account (RT) designation. Non-resident partners must also provide the CRA with identity documents and a Canadian contact or agent if required. If the LP has no physical presence in Canada, CRA may still issue a BN where the LP is carrying on a business in Canada through a deemed supply nexus. After the BN/RT account is active, the LP must file GST/HST returns electronically or by paper and maintain all supporting documentation for zero-rated exports.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible – An Alberta Limited Partnership is generally fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax purposes under subsection 96(1) of the Income Tax Act: the partnership is not a taxable entity; income, gains, losses, deductions and credits flow through to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement. However, for GST/HST purposes, the LP is treated as a separate registrant person under section 123 of the Excise Tax Act. With respect to foreign partners, the Canada–U.S. tax treaty and Canadian domestic hybrid rules may affect withholding and permanent establishment characterization. The LP itself remains a distinct GST/HST registrant for all taxable supplies made in or from Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a United States-style 'check-the-box' entity classification election. Entity classification is determined by provincial partnership law and CRA administrative interpretation. The LP and its partners may nonetheless make specific elections: (1) under subsection 97(2) of the Income Tax Act to transfer property to a partnership on a rollover basis at adjusted cost base; (2) under subsection 96(3) of the Income Tax Act to compute partnership income at the partnership level; and (3) for GST/HST, an election under section 273 of the Excise Tax Act to have a qualifying member or a designated member report and remit GST/HST on behalf of the partnership. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules in sections 18.4 to 18.6 and subsection 212.3(2) of the Income Tax Act may recharacterize certain payments or deny deductions if a partnership interest is structured with hybrid or fiscally transparent attributes inconsistent with Canadian tax policy.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Excise Tax Act (ETA). Alberta does not impose provincial sales tax and does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST); therefore, only the federal 5% GST applies in Alberta. For exported services and goods, a zero-rated (0%) indirect tax regime applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold: a person, including an Alberta LP, is a small supplier and is not required to register for GST/HST unless the value of its worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada (including those of associated persons and the preceding four-calendar-quarter lookback) exceeds CAD 30,000. A non-resident supplying CAD/BIM services into Canada may have mandatory registration if it is carrying on a tax supply nexus in Canada and exceeds this threshold. Voluntary registration is available to facilitate claiming input tax credits and zero-rating of exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time clearance or mandatory API fiscal stamping regime exists in Canada. The CRA does not operate a continuous transaction control or digital stamping system. Suppliers may issue electronic invoices provided they are readable, complete, and retain the required disclosure elements under subsection 221(1) of the ETA and section 286 of the ETA. Invoices must identify the supplier, recipient, the date, the supply amount, and the GST/HST charged or a declaration that the supply is zero-rated. EDI and electronic record-keeping systems are acceptable if accessible to CRA on request. For exported services, supplementary records must establish non-resident recipient status and offshore place-of-supply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: An Alberta LP supplying engineering, CAD, BIM, and structural drafting services to non-resident clients is eligible for zero-rating under Schedule VI, Part V (supplies to non-residents) of the Excise Tax Act where: (a) the recipient is a non-resident person; (b) the service is not supplied to an individual physically present in Canada; (c) the service is not performed in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed; and (d) the service is not a service that is to be performed wholly or partly in Canada in circumstances where the supply is not a supply of an advisory, consulting, or professional service made to a non-resident. Physical exports of drawings, models, or other tangible deliverables shipped out of Canada may also qualify under Schedule VI, Part VI or Part VII, provided the seller must export them (or cause them to be exported) as a condition of the supply. The supplier must retain contemporaneous commercial documentation, including invoices, contracts, and bank settlement evidence, to substantiate zero-rating at the time of audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency Form B13A or electronic CAED), where applicable for physical goods or media
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / multimodal carriage document
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign exchange bank confirmation evidencing receipt of payment from the non-resident buyer
Executed contract and commercial invoices identifying the non-resident purchaser, the services supplied, and the place of supply
Delivery and performance records, including BIM file transmission logs, engineering or drafting work product, and evidence of creation outside Canada or effective use outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may scrutinize export zero-rating claims through a GST/HST audit, verifying that the recipient is truly a non-resident, the services were not performed for Canadian real/personal property, and payment was received from abroad. If zero-rating is denied, the LP will be reassessed for 5% GST on the full invoice amount, plus interest under section 280 of the ETA. For false or negligent statements, a gross negligence penalty under section 285 of the ETA may be imposed in an amount up to 50% of the unreported tax. Fraudulent misrepresentation, falsification of documents, or deliberate concealment can lead to criminal prosecution under section 326 of the ETA and section 239 of the Income Tax Act, with fines and imprisonment. The normal four-year reassessment period may be extended indefinitely where the taxpayer has made a misrepresentation, omitted material facts, or committed fraud in filing the return. The LP remains liable to repay any input tax credits claimed on zero-rated supplies if supporting export documentation fails audit, and the partners may be jointly and severally liable for penalties and interest attributable to fraudulent or negligent partnership filings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility for both capital and current account transactions under the Bank of Canada Act. Profit remittances to foreign partners are permitted without prior approval but are subject to 25% withholding tax on dividends and mandatory FINTRAC reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Capital account transactions require no surrender but must comply with anti-money laundering and beneficial ownership verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement for surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts. All export transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC within prescribed timelines if involving cash or large-value movements. No fixed conversion ratios apply; repatriation occurs freely upon compliance with reporting obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for cross-border platforms such as Wise and Revolut, subject to full Canadian AML/KYC compliance and FINTRAC registration. Legal constraints include mandatory adherence to PCMLTFA for any offshore digital EMI activities involving Canadian LPs, with restrictions on anonymity features and source-of-funds verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote online opening and digital KYC permitted for Canadian LPs through verified identity platforms; physical presence of directors is not mandatory for standard onboarding but may be required for higher transaction volumes or complex beneficial ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership in high-risk jurisdictions or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide corporate charter, partnership agreement, beneficial ownership certificates, source of funds documentation, client contracts, and transaction history to substantiate legitimacy and mitigate red flags.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose codes 'CAP' or 'EQU'. Verification requires supporting documentation including partnership agreement, capital contribution records, beneficial ownership declarations, and audited financial statements. All transactions subject to FINTRAC reporting thresholds and corporate banking KYC protocols.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade settlements routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202. Commercial Letters of Credit available through domestic banks for larger infrastructure projects. All disbursements require proper invoice verification, AML screening, and alignment with engineering CAD outsourcing contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 25.00 per filing; continued failure may lead to administrative dissolution or strike-off by the Registrar under the Partnership Act (Alberta).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the day that is five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 per month for each partner (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); gross negligence penalties may also apply if omissions are intentional.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for a private limited partnership under the Partnership Act (Alberta). An audit becomes compulsory only if the LP is a 'reporting issuer' under the Alberta Securities Act, or if the partnership agreement or investor rights require an annual audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for reporting issuers; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for non-public partnerships. For tax purposes, the partnership's income is computed under the Income Tax Act using the accrual method, and the T5013 information return must reconcile accounting net income to partnership income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Partnership Act (Alberta) does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation requirement. The annual return filed with Service Alberta must update the list of general and limited partners. For FINTRAC purposes, the LP is considered a low-risk entity and is not a reporting entity unless it engages in regulated financial activities; nevertheless, prudent practice requires documenting partner identities and ownership percentages.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (contractually maintained, not royalty required)
Minute Book of Partner Resolutions and Consent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute; typical voluntary review or audit USD 2,500 - 7,500 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal + 8% Alberta general corporate = 23% combined; the Alberta limited partnership itself is fiscally transparent under ITA s.96, so the statutory rate applies at the partner, not LP, level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No Alberta export-processing or tax-holiday regime for CAD/BIM services. Relevant incentives: SR&ED 35% fully refundable investment tax credit on up to CAD 3M of eligible expenditures for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) and 15% non-refundable credit for non-CCPCs; Alberta small-business rate 2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; 20-year non-capital loss carryforward; no preferential rate for offshore engineering services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal) filed via CRA EFile/NETFILE-certified tax-transmission software; no separate Alberta LP tax return is required because the LP is not an Alberta corporate taxpayer.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013 is due five months after the LP's fiscal period-end (e.g., a December 31-year-end LP files by May 31 of the following calendar year); no federal extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) assigned to the Alberta limited partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A BN must be obtained before filing; non-resident partners should not file the T5013 under their own foreign tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period end date of the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the partnership's actual fiscal-year-end; Canadian-source income allocations to non-resident partners are taxed on this cut-off basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue for the partnership in Canadian dollars, including CAD/BIM drafting fees from foreign clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert all foreign-currency invoices at the Bank of Canada monthly average or noon spot rate; report in CAD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss after deductible expenses for the partnership's Canadian-source business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are taxable under ITA s.2(3) only on the Canadian-source share of the partnership's business income, not on gross billings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of each partner's share of income/loss, foreign-source income, capital gains, and withholding obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Issue T5013 slips to non-resident partners; do not treat profit allocations as dividends, but ensure any Part XIII amounts are separately reported and remitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T5013: CAD 100 per month per partner, with CRA penalty discretion under s.162(7); false filings trigger summary conviction fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment up to 12 months under s.238(2), plus gross-negligence penalties.
